definitions.explanation: The very highest or most important. Almost always used as a modifier before another noun to indicate that something is of the utmost level or importance.

examples.japanese: {安全|あんぜん}は{至上|しじょう}の{課題|かだい}だ。
この{会社|かいしゃ}では{顧客|こきゃく}{満足|まんぞく}を{至上|しじょう}{命令|めいれい}としている。
examples.english: This company treats customer satisfaction as its supreme directive.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}にとって{勝利|しょうり}こそが{至上|しじょう}の{喜|よろこ}びであり、そのためにすべてを{犠牲|ぎせい}にしてきた。
examples.english: For him, victory was the supreme joy, and he sacrificed everything for it.

notes:
Almost always used as a prefix-like modifier before a noun, not as a standalone predicate.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {至上|しじょう}{命令|めいれい} (supreme command/directive)
- {至上|しじょう}の{喜|よろこ}び (supreme joy)
- {至上|しじょう}の{目的|もくてき} (supreme objective)
- {至上|しじょう}{主義|しゅぎ} (supremacism — as in a doctrine)

Note the many homophones: {史上|しじょう} (in history), {市場|しじょう} (market), and {試乗|しじょう} (test drive) are all pronounced the same but written with different kanji.
